newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to pick partner for car plant by May 1.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to pick partner for car plant by May 1.

text.p: Ukraine will choose between General Motors Corp. and South Korea's Daewoo Group by May 1 for its investment partner in the AvtoZAZ car plant, a government spokesman said Friday.
"The government has ordered the commission to find a consultant by March 1 and to inform the government which investment project is better by May 1," the spokesman said.

An investment tender to find a strategic investor for AvtoZAZ was officially announced earlier this month. Economics Minister Vasyl Hureyev is heading a commission to oversee the tender, which has received proposals from GM and Daewoo.
Ukraine has been seeking a strategic investor for AvtoZAZ, Ukraine's only car plant, for two years.
Officials say the plant, in the eastern industrial city of Zaporizhya, needs about $1 billion of investment over the next few years.
AvtoZAZ produced 6,881 small Tavria and Dana cars last year against 130,000 units in 1992. Its capacity is 150,000 units.
Tender rules require the investment partner to continue production of Ukrainian cars.
The size of the AvtoZAZ stake for sale is negotiable between 26 and 51 percent, government sources said.

They said GM foresaw two stages of restructuring. The first would see annual output of Opel Vectras rise to 25,000 per year, alongside production of between 70,000 and 80,000 Tavrias. Opel production would increase to 40,000 in a second stage.
Daewoo, which said in December it was ready to invest about $1 billion in AvtoZAZ, has proposed annual output of 100,000 Tavrias and assembly of three Daewoo models within 18 months.
